header.running_head: The Hijrah of Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Some Other Sahabah (RA)

blocks.text: Gratitude is incumbent on us as long as a caller calls to Allaah" [^1]
The Hijrah of Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Some Other Sahabah (RA)
The First Person to Migrate from Makkah to Madinah

Hadhrat Baraa bin Aazib (RA) says, "The first Muslims (from Makkah) to migrate to us (in Madinah) were Hadhrat Mus'ab bin Umayr (RA) and Hadhrat Ibn Ummu Maktoom (RA). The two of them started teaching us the Qur'aan. Thereafter, Hadhrat Ammaar, Bilaal and Sa'd (RA) migrated, followed by Hadhrat Umar (RA) accompanied by twenty others. I have never seen the people of Madinah happier on any occasion than the occasion when they arrived. By the time they arrived, I had already learnt Surah A'la amongst other Mufassal Surahs." [^2]

Another narration states that Hadhrat Baraa bin Aazib (RA) said, "The first from amongst the Muhaajireen to come to us was Hadhrat Mus'ab bin Umayr (RA) who belonged to the Banu Abdid Daar tribe. Then came Hadhrat Ibn Ummu Maktoom (RA) who was a blind man belonging to the Banu Fihr tribe. Thereafter, Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) arrived with twenty mounted men. When we asked him what had happened to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he said that Rasulullaah ﷺ was coming after him. Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) arrived afterwards. By the time Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived, I had already learnt several Surahs from the Mufassal Surahs." [^3]
The Hijrah of Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) and his Two Companions

Hadhrat Umar (RA) says, "When I decided to migrate to Madinah, Ayaash bin Abi Rabee'ah, Hishaam bin Aas and I arranged to meet at the valley of Tanaadhib which was a place after Sarif at the oasis of the Banu Ghifaar tribe. We agreed that if any of us was not there by dawn, it meant that he was stopped and the other two were to proceed. Consequently, Ayaash and I were at Tanaadhib by dawn and Hishaam was prevented from coming. He was put in difficulty (by the Mushrikeen) and he succumbed to it (forsook Islaam). When we arrived in Madinah, we stayed with the Banu Amr bin Awf tribe at Quba. Ayaash was the cousin and uterine brother of Abu Jahal bin Hishaam and Haarith bin Hishaam. The two of them therefore came for him in Madinah (to take him back to Makkah) at a time when Rasulullaah ﷺ was still in Makkah."
The two of them spoke to Ayaash and said, 'Your mother has taken a vow never to comb her hair and never to take shade from the sun until she sees you.'
Bayhaqi as quoted in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.3 Pg.197).
Ibn Abi Shaybah as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.331).
Ahmad. Bukhari and Muslim have also narrated it as quoted in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.3 Pg.188).
